decision_table.name: Determine_MO_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Missouri state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in Missouri (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets Missouri economic nexus threshold ($100,000 gross receipts)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
Missouri filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in Missouri if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in MO - Employees working in MO - Tangible personal property located in MO - Real property located in MO
Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 32.200 (Nexus and apportionment) Reference: Missouri Form MO-1120 Instructions

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
Missouri filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts from Missouri customers.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), Missouri requires filing if a corporation exceeds the economic nexus threshold, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: Missouri Department of Revenue Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 144.605 (Economic nexus provisions)

No Missouri nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 32.200 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_MO_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate Missouri state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income. Includes Missouri's unique 50% federal income tax deduction.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
Missouri state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
MISSOURI ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to MO) - IRC Section 199A qualified business income deduction addback (MO does not conform) - State income taxes deducted on federal return - Bonus depreciation addback (varies by tax year) - Expenses related to exempt income
MISSOURI SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - 50% OF FEDERAL INCOME TAX PAID (UNIQUE MISSOURI FEATURE) * This is a significant benefit that reduces Missouri taxable income * Calculated as: federal_tax_liability × 50% * One of only a few states that still allow federal tax deductibility * Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 143.121 - Interest on Missouri state and municipal bonds - Missouri net operating loss deduction (subject to MO limitations) - Certain dividend income (depends on circumstances)
The 50% federal tax deduction is Missouri's most distinctive corporate tax feature. It significantly reduces the effective Missouri tax burden compared to other states with similar rates.
Example calculation: - Federal taxable income: $1,000,000 - Federal tax (21%): $210,000 - Missouri 50% federal tax deduction: $105,000 - Missouri taxable income: $1,000,000 - $105,000 = $895,000 - Missouri tax (4.0%): $35,800 - Effective Missouri rate: 3.58% (instead of 4.0%)
Reference: Missouri Form MO-1120 Schedule A (Additions to Federal Taxable Income) Reference: Missouri Form MO-1120 Schedule B (Deductions from Federal Taxable Income) Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 143.121 (50% federal tax deduction) Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 143.141 (Adjustments to federal taxable income)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have Missouri nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_MO_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate Missouri state corporate income tax. Applies Missouri 4.0% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income. Missouri's unique 50% federal tax deduction significantly reduces effective tax burden.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
Missouri state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to Missouri: × [MO apportionment percentage] 3. Missouri additions: + [Federal interest, IRC 199A addback, etc.] 4. Missouri subtractions: - [50% federal tax, MO municipal interest, MO NOL, etc.] 5. Missouri taxable income: = [Result] 6. Missouri tax rate: × 4.0% flat rate 7. Missouri income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. Missouri credits: - [Jobs, historic preservation, film, neighborhood, etc.] 9. Missouri tax liability: = [Final tax]
Missouri uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
UNIQUE MISSOURI ADVANTAGE: The 50% federal income tax deduction significantly reduces the effective tax burden: - Nominal rate: 4.0% - Effective rate: ~3.6% (after 50% federal tax deduction benefit)
This makes Missouri's effective corporate tax rate among the lowest in states with income taxes, despite the 4.0% nominal rate being in the middle of the pack.
Example effective rate calculation: - Federal taxable income: $1,000,000 - Federal tax (21%): $210,000 - MO 50% federal tax deduction: -$105,000 - MO taxable income: $895,000 - MO tax (4.0%): $35,800 - Effective MO rate: 3.58% of federal taxable income
Missouri tax rate history: - 2025: 4.0% flat rate - Prior years: 4.0% flat rate (consistent) - Federal tax deduction: Long-standing Missouri feature
Missouri provides various tax credits including: - Quality Jobs Program tax credit - Historic Preservation tax credit - Film Production tax credit - Neighborhood Preservation tax credit - New Markets tax credit
Reference: Missouri Form MO-1120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 143.071 (Tax rate of 4.0%) Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 143.121 (50% federal tax deduction) Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 32.200 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: Missouri Department of Revenue Corporate Tax Guidance

No Missouri nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in Missouri. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 32.200 (Nexus requirements)

No Missouri taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has Missouri nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments (including 50% federal tax deduction). Any estimated payments are refunded.
Missouri net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - Missouri allows NOL carryforward - NOL deduction subject to Missouri limitations - Carryforward period generally follows federal rules with MO modifications
The 50% federal tax deduction can create situations where Missouri taxable income is zero or negative even when federal taxable income is positive, resulting in no Missouri tax liability.
Reference: Missouri Form MO-1120 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Missouri Revised Statutes § 143.151 (Net operating loss deduction)
